values.note: Forest Service dispersed camping: no reservations. 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period.' Keep the campsite within 150 ft of the road and at least 100 ft from water; 'Dispersed camping is not allowed in the vicinity of developed recreation areas such as campgrounds, picnic areas, or trailheads.'

booking.source: https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/camping-cabins (Dispersed Camping: 'Recreationist can camp anywhere in the National Forest outside a designated campground', 'Dispersed camping in one location is allowable up to 14 days in any 30-day period'), read 2026-10-21

values.note: Dispersed site: the Forest Service says to 'Expect little to no facilities, restrooms, trash removal, fire pits and picnic tables.'

summary: No Forest Service page exists for Big Bend itself (no fs.usda.gov page found; the entry has no website). The George Washington & Jefferson NF's forest-wide dispersed-camping rules confirm no reservations, free dispersed camping, and add the 14-days-in-30 limit. Fees (free) left as they are. Not stated anywhere official: anything specific to this site.
flags: Criteria lead (human decides): the GW&J dispersed rules say 'Dispersed camping is not allowed in the vicinity of developed recreation areas such as campgrounds, picnic areas, or trailheads' (https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/camping-cabins), and the entry's inclusion evidence describes the spot as an 'old picnic area' (Wikipedia's Seven Sisters article says the Big Bend picnic area 'has become an overlook'). Whether overnighting at the Big Bend overlook is allowed is not stated by the Forest Service. The inclusion's '3-day limit' and site details come from TMBtent/boondocking listings only.
Missing website: no official page for this site; the forest-wide rules page is https://www.fs.usda.gov/r08/gwj/recreation/camping-cabins.
